key_insight: An interpretable hybrid model encoded the Alzheimer’s A/T/N biomarker framework as logic rules while using neural networks to extract biomarker features, aiming to predict incident AD more flexibly than purely rule-based or purely data-driven methods.
clinical_relevance: This approach may improve early risk stratification for Alzheimer’s disease years before symptoms appear, while keeping model decisions more transparent for research use.
method: Encoded the A/T/N framework as a logic program
Used one or more neural networks to extract input biomarker features
Combined interpretability with data-driven prediction in the ADNI dataset
evidence_signal: In ADNI, the pipeline predicted four-year incident Alzheimer’s disease with sensitivity up to 0.84 and learned relative importance scores for A/T/N profiles.
watch_item: The learned scores suggested empirically derived A and T cutoffs may not generalize well to ADNI, so threshold choices may need revalidation across cohorts.
paper_title: Encoding Discordance in the Alzheimer's Disease A/T/N Framework
